title: The Map to the Rainbow Wall
markdown:
Weekend sun, warm like butter, streamed through the leafy canopy of the giant oak and made dancing patterns on the wooden floor of the Curiosity Canopy, the best treehouse ever. Saffron the giraffe, her neck as long and elegant as a question mark, peered into a dusty old book. Beside her, Bix the monkey bounced on a rope swing, a whirlwind of busy energy. Hettie the parrot, emerald and sapphire feathers, preened with tiny precise pecks.

“What grand adventure awaits us today?” Bix chattered, voice fizzing like a lemonade bottle about to pop. “We’ve polished the spyglasses till they shine like dragon’s eyes! Sorted our acorns by size and shininess! Invented a handshake with seven wiggles!”

Saffron nudged a faded crinkled parchment from the back of the book. “Look at this. It seems to have been hiding.”

Wiggly lines. Dots like spilled pepper. Symbols that looked like secrets whispered on paper.

“Ooh, a map!” Bix’s eyes widened like saucers. “Treasure hoard! Gold doubloons! Glittering jewels! Maybe even a pirate’s lost sock!”

Hettie tilted her head. “Squawk! Treasure! Shiny!” Her voice was surprisingly deep for such a small bird.

Saffron traced a peculiar symbol with a long gentle finger. “I’m not so sure it’s a treasure map in the way you imagine. These look less like directions and more like instructions. A wobbly line. Three dots in a neat row. They don’t point to a specific spot.”

“Nonsense!” Bix snatched the map, enthusiasm as bouncy as ever. “It clearly points to the grand old oak by the school gates! I bet there’s a fat X under the roots!” He grabbed a small rusty spade, ready to dig.

They were about to clamber down when a loud indignant squawk shattered the afternoon from the school fence below. “A map! They have a map!” Heledd Bumble, self-appointed leader of the Grumble-Snouts—a gang from the other side of town who considered themselves the ultimate rivals—had a booming voice and an even louder desire to be first, best, and most victorious at everything. Beside her, the team shuffled, looking unusually shifty.

“Oh, fiddle-dee-dee,” Hettie muttered, imitating Heledd’s high-pitched demanding voice. “They’ve got a map!”

Saffron’s mind, usually calm, began to buzz. “Bix, Hettie, we must go. But we’ll have to be clever. Heledd thinks it’s about digging for gold. I have a feeling it’s a riddle.”

The race was on. The Curiosity Canopy crew scrambled down the rope ladder, Bix a blur of brown fur. The Grumble-Snouts followed, mismatched T-shirts and determined grumbles, Heledd barking orders like a bellowing bullfrog. They burst onto the sun-drenched school field, the map clutched in Saffron’s hoof.

The first symbol, a distinctively wobbly line, guided them toward the ancient moss-covered bell tower. “The clue must be up there!” Bix was already halfway up the scaffolding. Saffron followed, long legs stretching. Hettie fluttered beside them, a tiny colourful commentator squawking snippets of Heledd’s frantic instructions. Inside the dusty echoing tower, cobwebs like ghostly lace, they found chalk markings: three dots in a neat triangle.

“That’s it.” A spark in Saffron’s eyes. “Not a place. A pattern.” She drew the triangle on the map.

Heledd and crew arrived panting. “What are you doing up there? Where’s the hidden X?”

“This way!” Saffron pointed toward the colourful playground. The next symbol looked like a wiggly worm. On the climbing frame, almost hidden, a chalk worm, and beside it a radiant sun, a fluffy cloud, a cheerful smiley face.

“Sun, cloud, smiley face,” Bix pondered, scratching his head. “A very happy day?”

Hettie, perched on Saffron’s head, squawked with delight. “Squawk! Happy weather!”

“A sunny day with a few fluffy clouds.” Saffron drew it on the map.

Meanwhile Heledd’s crew dug with wild abandon under the school gates. “Nothing here but mud and very surprised earthworms!” one whined, throwing down a spade.

The final symbol was a dramatic swirl. “That looks just like the big mural on the art classroom.” They raced, Grumble-Snouts hot on their heels.

At the mural—a vast expanse of painted colour—chalk marks were smudged and faded. A rogue football, kicked with more enthusiasm than accuracy, whizzed past Bix’s nose like a startled bee. He yelped, stumbled, dropped the map. Heledd snatched it with the lightning speed of a hungry squirrel.

“Ha! We’ve got it! You silly, silly creatures! This map is completely useless!” She waved it. A mischievous gust snatched it toward a muddy puddle. Heledd’s team leader tripped, somersaulted, landed splat beside the mural. The map tore. A corner came away. He stared at the blank space on the wall, then at the scrap, face falling like a deflated balloon. “It’s… just a bit of wall now.”

The Grumble-Snouts stomped off, muttering about wasted Saturdays, glittering gold unfound. Saffron, Bix, and Hettie sat by the blank mural, torn fragment on the dewy grass. Bix’s bottom lip trembled. “We didn’t find any treasure. It was all just pretend.”

Saffron’s long neck drooped. She looked at the remaining symbols—wobbly line, three dots, sun, cloud, smiley—then at the blank section. Not a hunt. A design. Not to find. To make.

“Heledd was wrong. This isn’t about finding treasure. It’s about making it.” She pointed a slender hoof. “The wobbly line can be the river. The three dots, twinkling stars. Sun, cloud, smiley—that’s for the sky.”

They scrambled up. Forgotten tubs of brightly coloured chalk from the art classroom’s open window, dust tickling noses. Bix scrambled the wall, monkey grip sure. Hettie on his shoulder like a colourful captain, sharp clear instructions. Saffron drew the bolder sweeping lines.

A shimmering cerulean river. Twinkling chalk stars. A cheerful golden sun. Fluffy white clouds. A giant happy smiley that seemed to radiate glee.

They stepped back. Ms. Primrose the Headteacher walked past, stopped, eyes widening. She looked at the mural, then at three chalk-smudged friends. “Goodness me. What a truly wonderful creation.” She examined the fragment still in Saffron’s hoof, thoughtful rather than lecturing, and left them the quiet of their own pride.

Heledd and the Grumble-Snouts, who had peeked back around the corner, stared, mouths hanging open.

Later, in the Curiosity Canopy, the crew shared warm crumbly cookies and gazed out at the mural. The school had gathered to admire it. Bix was already sketching something on a spare leaf. Hettie, perched on Saffron’s head, let out a contented squawk. Butter-warm sun still made dancing patterns on the treehouse floor—the same patterns as the morning, now thrown also, faintly, from a wall they had filled themselves.
characters: Saffron (a giraffe), Bix (a monkey), Hettie (a parrot)
